info.name: Vimas - User (Buyer & Merchant)
info.description: Buyer and merchant-facing APIs for the Vimas e-commerce backend. Run "Register" (username + password, optionally referred_username) to create an account and auto-populate {{token}} and {{refresh_token}} — no email verification is required. Afterwards call "Update Profile" to add first/last name, email, address, country, and phone number. Use "Login (Username)" to sign back in, or "Refresh Token" once the access token expires.

request.description: Returns { uploadUrl, fileUrl }. PUT the raw file bytes directly to uploadUrl (with a matching Content-Type header, no auth) within 5 minutes — the presigned URL expires after that. fileUrl is the permanent CloudFront URL to store/display once the upload completes. Any authenticated user or admin token works — this endpoint isn't role-gated.

type=reseller restricts results to bulk-purchasable products (bulk_available = 1). Omit (or any other value) to get the full catalog. Points display: for consumer/default, each product includes totalPoints (if the product's showTotalPoints is on) and pointsSharing (if showPointsSharing is on) sourced from the product itself. For type=reseller, those same two fields instead come from EACH active bulk package under the product — returned as bulkPointsSharing: an array of { productBulkDetailsId, packageQuantity, totalPoints?, pointsSharing? }, one entry per package, each gated by that package's own showTotalPoints/showPointsSharing.

Response conditionally includes totalPoints/pointsSharing — an array of { receiverType, pointsPercentage, points } for each active BUY_PRODUCT distribution rule — sourced from the product's own showTotalPoints/showPointsSharing for consumer/default requests. type=reseller returns "Product not found" unless the product's bulk_available = 1, and swaps those fields for bulkPointsSharing: one entry per active bulk package ( { productBulkDetailsId, packageQuantity, totalPoints?, pointsSharing? } ), each gated by that package's own showTotalPoints/showPointsSharing instead of the product's.
Likes the product if you haven't liked it yet, unlikes it if you have. Returns { liked, likeCount } — likeCount is recomputed from product_likes (COUNT), then written back to products.like_count.
Returns whether you've liked this product plus the current likeCount.

Records a view for this product from the current user. Repeat views from the same user touch last_viewed_at rather than counting again, so view_count is unique-viewer count. GET /products/:id already calls this internally on every visit — this endpoint exists for cases where you want to record a view without fetching the full product payload (e.g. a carousel/quick-view widget).
Returns just id + packageQuantity + unitPrice per active package — enough to render a "buy N units" picker.
Full product_bulk_details row for the package the buyer picked from the list above, scoped to that product.

cart_type is optional and defaults to "consumer". consumer and reseller are separate rows for the same product — adding a reseller line for a product you already have as consumer creates a second row instead of merging quantities. quantity is checked against consumerMinimumQuantity/consumerMaximumQuantity (or resellerMinimumQuantity/resellerMaximumQuantity for reseller) — 400 if outside those bounds. For cart_type="reseller", productBulkDetailsId is required — see the "Add To Cart (Reseller)" request for how multiple packages of the same product are handled.

Each distinct productBulkDetailsId is its own cart row — adding package #2 after already having package #1 in your cart creates a SECOND reseller row, it does not overwrite the first. Adding the same productBulkDetailsId again just increases that row's quantity. Either way, resellerMinimumQuantity/resellerMaximumQuantity bounds the TOTAL quantity across every reseller row you hold for this product (i.e. every package you've picked, counted together) — a package counts as "quantity 1" toward that cap regardless of how many units are physically inside it. productBulkDetailsId must reference an active product_bulk_details package for this exact product (see the Product Bulk Details folder).

cart_type disambiguates which of your rows for this product to update (defaults to "consumer"). For cart_type="reseller", productBulkDetailsId is REQUIRED — it identifies which specific package's row to update, since a reseller product can have more than one row (one per package). quantity sets that row's value directly (not additive); it's validated against the same consumer/reseller min-max bounds as Add To Cart, applied to the TOTAL across all of your rows for this product+type, not just this one row.

cart_type query param disambiguates which of your rows for this product to remove (defaults to "consumer"). For cart_type=reseller, productBulkDetailsId is REQUIRED — it identifies which specific package's row to remove, so removing one package doesn't wipe every reseller row you have for this product.

Returns every cart row for the buyer — one consumer row per product at most, and for reseller, one row per distinct bulk package picked (so the same product can appear multiple times as reseller rows, each with its own productBulkDetails).

request.description: Creates one pending order per cart item and returns a Stripe Checkout URL. Redirect the buyer to data.checkoutUrl.

item.name: Check Order Status By Stripe Session

request.description: Frontend polls this after Stripe redirects back with ?session_id=... to confirm payment status.

Each product's isOutOfStock is true if either the admin flagged it out of stock, OR you (the requesting user) have already redeemed maximumQuantity of it — in that case purchasedQuantity/maxPurchaseReached explain why, so the frontend can hide/disable the buy button instead of showing a generic "out of stock".

Response includes currentPointsBalance and canAfford — an upfront preview of whether you have enough points, based on minimumQuantity. isOutOfStock is true if either the admin flagged it out of stock, OR you've already redeemed maximumQuantity of it (see purchasedQuantity/maxPurchaseReached) — canAfford factors this in too. The actual check happens again (authoritatively) when you call Redeem Product.

Debits pointPrice x quantity from your PointUserBalance. maximumQuantity is a per-user lifetime cap, not just a per-request bound — this sums every purchase you've already made of this reward and rejects (400) if this request would push you over the cap, even if this individual request's quantity is within bounds. Also 400 if you don't have enough points or the product is out of stock; 404 if the product doesn't exist or isn't active.
Lazily creates a zeroed balance row on first call if the buyer/merchant has none yet.

Full referral downline tree. Each node shows earnedForMe (points earned directly from that member's own purchases) and subtreeTotal (earnedForMe + everyone below them). Response also includes a totalDownlineEarnings grand total.

Wallet snapshot, current-month earned/redeemed points, REFERRAL_LEVEL_1/REFERRAL_LEVEL_2 reward counts + totals, and trend — the last 6 calendar months (oldest first, including the current in-progress month) as [{ m, purchases, points }]: m is the month abbreviation (e.g. "Feb"), purchases is the count of this buyer's paid orders (payment_status_id = 2) that month, points is the sum of points credited to their wallet that month. Months with no activity come back as 0, not omitted, so the array is always 6 entries long.
Omit rating (and set parentFeedbackId) to post a reply to another feedback/comment instead of a top-level review.
Soft-deletes (status becomes 'deleted') so replies/likes from other users are preserved.
